title: Calcium Imaging of Cultured Cells with Fluo-4 Using Nikon Automated Microscopy
author: Akihiro Suto

steps.title: Prepare Microscope and Incubator
steps.instruction: Prepare the imaging environment and hardware to maintain cell viability and temperature.

substeps.instruction: Preheat the stage/cage incubator to 37°C 1-2 hours before imaging.
Flush the incubation chamber with CO2 10-20 minutes before imaging, ensuring the correct holder is used and no large openings allow CO2 to escape.
Place the chamber slide on the microscope stage.
Select an objective for the required magnification (typically a 20x Air objective; immersion media objectives are preferred for >20x, though an objective heater may be necessary).

steps.title: Configure Acquisition Parameters
steps.instruction: Set the camera and light settings to optimize for high-speed calcium imaging.

substeps.instruction: Set the exposure to 10ms or less (recommended at least 100FPS for cardiomyocytes).
Crop the camera sensor to a smaller region of interest (ROI) to increase framerate; note that cropping height increases framerate, while cropping width does not.

steps.title: Position and Focus Sample
steps.instruction: Locate the sample and stabilize the focus.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to the center of the well and focus on the sample.
Optional: Search for the perfect focus system (PFS) offset and activate PFS to stabilize against thermal fluctuations and maintain focus.

steps.title: Configure JOB File and Channels
steps.instruction: Set up the automated imaging sequence and channel selection.

substeps.instruction: Import the JOB definition .bin file (e.g., Multipoint Calcium Imaging.bin) into JOBs Explorer.
Select the appropriate imaging channel (e.g., Green channel for Fluo-4).
Set the number of timelapse recordings based on experimental requirements or well size.
Set the duration of each individual recording.
Verify that the sample is still in focus.
